newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-GILLESPIE DESTROYS BORDER WITH CAREER BEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GILLESPIE DESTROYS BORDER WITH CAREER BEST.

text.p: Fast bowler Jason Gillespie returned career best figures of seven for 34 as Australia routed Border for 117 on the first day of their three-day game at Buffalo Park on Friday.
Mark Waugh then stroked a typically elegant 62 from 59 deliveries as the touring team reached 206 for five by the close - a lead of 89.
Paul Reiffel and Andy Bichel shared the new ball once Ian Healy won the toss and chose to bowl first, but Gillespie had things entirely his way when he came on as first change after 14 overs.
The 21-year-old South Australian took six successive wickets after Reiffel had removed opener Piet Botha in the first over of the match, courtesy of Mark Waugh's catch at first slip.

Healy claimed a brace of victims off Gillespie while Greg Blewett and Matthew Elliott both held catches at third slip. Gillespie's figures easily surpassed his previous best first-class return of six for 68 against Western Australia last year.

One man who did not fall to Gillespie was 41-year-old Peter Kirsten, playing his last match before retirement. The former South African captain was hoping to end a career spanning 25 years with his 58th first- class century but he edged Reiffel to Elliott at third slip for just seven.

Elliott then made a solid 41 on a well-grassed but trustworthy pitch and Waugh included nine sumptuous boundaries and one towering straight six in his 62 as Australia confirmed their domination of outclassed opponents.
